name: Graft
text:
Decision: We should build a single, living “memory map” document that links every key idea to its meaning, its neighbors, and the concrete things it helps us recall.

Why: A map lets us see how facts connect instead of storing them in isolation, which is exactly what “recall by meaning” needs. It also grows with us—new ideas plug in where they fit, so nothing stays unembedded.

Trade-off: We give up the speed of quick look-ups in favor of deeper, lasting understanding. The map takes time to build and maintain, but that time is an investment in memory that pays off every time we use it.
